[[Category:Artificial neural network]]
[[Category:Large language models]]
'''Self-attention''' relates the positions of a sequence to one another, so that each position's representation is built from the whole sequence rather than from a fixed window.<ref>{{#cite:Q3130}}</ref>

== Definition ==

Let $\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d}$ hold the representations of the $T$ positions in its rows, and let $\mathbf{W}_Q,\mathbf{W}_K,\mathbf{W}_V\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d_k}$ be learned projections. The queries, keys, and values are

$$
\mathbf{Q}=\mathbf{X}\mathbf{W}_Q,
\qquad
\mathbf{K}=\mathbf{X}\mathbf{W}_K,
\qquad
\mathbf{V}=\mathbf{X}\mathbf{W}_V.
$$

Each position scores itself against every other through a scaled dot product, and averages the values by the resulting weights,

$$
\operatorname{Attention}(\mathbf{Q},\mathbf{K},\mathbf{V})
=
\operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^{\top}}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)\mathbf{V},
$$

where the [[Softmax|softmax]] is taken row-wise, and the factor $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ keeps the scores from growing with the dimension.

== Causal masking ==

A decoder must not see later positions, so the scores above the diagonal are suppressed before the softmax,

$$
\mathbf{A}
=
\operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^{\top}}{\sqrt{d_k}}+\mathbf{M}\right),
\qquad
M_{jk}=
\begin{cases}
0, & j\ge k, \\
-\infty, & j<k,
\end{cases}
$$

so that position $j$ attends only to positions $k\le j$. This mask is what makes the output of position $j$ predictable from $x_{1:j}$ alone, and hence what allows a sequence to be generated one token at a time.

== Complexity ==

The score matrix $\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^{\top}$ is $T\times T$, so attention over a context of length $T$ costs $\mathcal{O}(T^2d)$ time and $\mathcal{O}(T^2)$ memory. Generating a sequence recomputes most of this work unless the keys and values already computed are kept, which is the purpose of [[KV caching]].
